subject: Segmented retention & redaction playbook for EHR connector
messages:
From: Lisa Huang <lisa.huang@lakeviewhealth.org>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: security@lakeviewhealth.org
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask: retention windows + redaction options for EHR connector

Diego,

Thanks for the quick call yesterday. Lakeview is preparing a pilot to ingest de-identified visit notes from our outpatient EHR into a Redwood-hosted inference pipeline. Two immediate asks from our security and privacy teams:

1) We need recommended retention limits that balance analytics usefulness with PHI minimization for a 90-day pilot and potential production. Are you able to provide guidance for short (30d), medium (90d), and long (365d) options plus risks?

2) For fields considered direct identifiers (MRN, SSN, full name), what redaction strategies do you support out of the box versus ones that would require customization? Specifically: reversible tokenization, deterministic pseudonymization, irreversible hashing/salting, and field-level masking.

Also please include how deletion works across backups and replicas — Lakeview needs a proof point for our auditors that we can achieve tenant-scoped erasure within an agreed SLA.

Appreciate any playbook or config snippets you can share.

Best,
Lisa Huang
Lead, Information Security
Lakeview Health

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Lisa Huang <lisa.huang@lakeviewhealth.org>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: retention windows + redaction options for EHR connector

Lisa — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; attaching a short playbook (redaction-playbook-v1.0.pdf) and a sample config.

Retention recommendations (quick):
- Short (30d): best for high-sensitivity pilots where only immediate QA is needed — we recommend field-level masking for all direct identifiers and a 30d automatic purge of raw blobs.
- Medium (90d): balances model tuning vs privacy; keep tokenized identifiers for linkage only, with deterministic pseudonyms and strict access controls; encrypt at-rest with customer-managed KMS.
- Long (365d): for advanced analytics; use irreversible hashing for SSN/MRN with per-customer salt + strong key rotation policy, and store linkage tables inside the customer VPC (Private deployment).

Redaction options we support:
- Field-level masking (configurable) — out-of-the-box.
- Deterministic pseudonymization (e.g., "patient_0001") — out-of-the-box for hosted & dedicated, with option to bring your salt key for private deployments.
- Reversible tokenization (vaulted tokens) — available as a paid add-on; tokens held in a separate keystore (recommended if you need to rehydrate for QA).
- Irreversible hashing (SHA-256 + salt) — supported; we strongly recommend per-customer salt management.

Deletion behavior and verification:
- Tenant-scoped delete triggers cascade to primary store, KV caches, and async purge jobs for secondary replicas. Metadata and audit logs retained per default (90d) unless customer requests shorter retention.
- Backups: automated snapshots are retained per backup policy; we offer a backup-expunge flow that schedules a verified purge of snapshots within the deletion SLA for Dedicated and Private customers. Hosted API customers can request snapshot purge; timing depends on snapshot schedule but we provide certification when done.
- Verification: we provide an erasable token and a deletion report (hashes of removed objects) and can run a cryptographic evidence routine for auditors.

I'll loop Rishi and Monica for implementation details and to confirm deletion SLAs for hosted vs dedicated.

Next steps:
- Share sample config (attached) and playbook.
- Rishi to confirm snapshot purge windows and timeline (owned by infra).
- Diego to provide an auditor-friendly deletion report template.

Regards,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Lisa Huang <lisa.huang@lakeviewhealth.org>, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: retention windows + redaction options for EHR connector

Lisa — quick infra note from my side:
- For Hosted customers, our standard backup cadence is daily snapshots with 30-day retention. We can run a snapshot-expunge (manual/automated) but a SLA-backed guaranteed window requires Dedicated or Private.
- For Dedicated, we can commit to a 48-hour verified purge of primary + replicas + snapshot expunge after an authorized deletion request, and provide the verification report.
- For Private deployments (VPC/on-prem), the customer owns snapshots and expunge; we provide the tooling and a playbook to generate the deletion evidence.

On pseudonymization vs hashing: if you need reversible mapping for dedup/QA, use deterministic pseudonyms with a customer salt; otherwise irreversible hashing reduces re-identification risk and simplifies audit.

I'll add a short infra appendix to the playbook clarifying timelines and what we can certify under each deployment model.

Thanks,
Rishi
Principal Infrastructure Engineer

From: Lisa Huang <lisa.huang@lakeviewhealth.org>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: retention windows + redaction options for EHR connector

Thanks Diego and Rishi — this helps. A couple of follow-ups from our auditors:

1) Can you confirm the exact artifacts in a deletion report? They asked for: object identifiers removed, cryptographic hashes before deletion, timestamps, and the operator ID who triggered the workflow.
2) For the reversible tokenization option, what is the token lifetime and where are the keys stored? They prefer HSM-backed KMS with key rotation every 180 days.

If you can send a short sample deletion report and the infra appendix, we can determine whether Hosted is acceptable for our pilot or if we should plan a Dedicated proof-of-concept.

Regards,
Lisa

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Lisa Huang <lisa.huang@lakeviewhealth.org>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: retention windows + redaction options for EHR connector

Lisa — attaching the playbook + sample-redaction-config.yaml (see attachments). Quick answers inline:

1) Deletion report artifacts: list of object IDs (UUIDs), SHA-256 of deleted blobs, deletion request timestamp, purge job completion timestamp, operator/service account ID, and an audit signature (HMAC) we sign for verification. We include a JSONL-style sample report in the playbook.

2) Reversible tokenization: tokens issued with TTL configurable (default 90 days). Keys are stored in customer-managed KMS where available (Dedicated/Private); for Hosted we use HSM-backed managed KMS and can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) on request. We support rotation cadence you specified (180 days) and will generate a rotation trace in the deletion report.

Recommend next step: short joint working session (30–45m) with Lakeview security and our infra team (Rishi + Monica) to walk the playbook and align on whether Hosted pilot with snapshot-expunge request meets your auditors or if Dedicated is required.

Proposed times: Wed 10/21 10:00–10:45 PT or Thu 10/22 13:30–14:15 PT. Let me know which works and I will send a calendar invite + HubSpot record (HS-6227).

Regards,
Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
